42743912.summary: Evidence suggests that higher whole-grain intake is associated with lower cardiometabolic disease risks, although underlying mechanisms remain unclear. The authors performed a random-effects meta-analysis of randomized trials to evaluate the effects of whole grains on cardiometabolic risk factors. Mean differences with 95% confidence intervals were estimated per 48 g/day increment of whole grains in dry weight, equivalent to approximately 90 g or 3 servings of fresh weight. The analysis included 87 trials across 101 publications. Each 48 g/day increment of whole-grain intake was associated with a reduction in body weight of -0.20 kg (95% CI: -0.31 to -0.09; n = 41) with high certainty. Reductions with high certainty were also observed for waist circumference (-0.22 cm; 95% CI: -0.39 to -0.06; n = 27) and total cholesterol (-0.10 mmol/L; 95% CI: -0.13 to -0.07; n = 54). Interleukin-6 was reduced by -0.12 pg/mL (95% CI: -0.23 to -0.00; n = 12) with high certainty. Moderate certainty evidence demonstrated reductions in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of -0.07 mmol/L (95% CI: -0.10 to -0.05; n = 52) and triglycerides of -0.04 mmol/L (95% CI: -0.06 to -0.02; n = 52). Reductions with moderate certainty were also noted for fasting plasma glucose (-0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI: -0.06 to -0.00; n = 44) and systolic blood pressure (-0.82 mmHg; 95% CI: -1.49 to -0.15; n = 32). Non-linear analyses indicated the greatest effects occurred at 60-100 g/day for most outcomes, whereas a few outcomes showed maximal effects at higher intakes up to 180-220 g/day. Safety outcomes and adverse events were not reported in the abstract. Study limitations noted by the authors include varying certainty of evidence across outcomes and sparse data at higher intake levels limiting firm conclusions regarding dose thresholds. The authors conclude that whole-grain consumption improves multiple cardiometabolic risk factors, with larger effects generally observed at 60-100 g/day.
42743912.relation_evidence: Higher whole-grain consumption has been broadly associated in nutritional epidemiology with lower rates of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. This study synthesizes randomized trial data to quantify the effect size and dose-response relationship of whole-grain intake on intermediate cardiometabolic markers.
42743912.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42743912.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that whole-grain intake was associated with improvements in multiple cardiometabolic risk factors, with larger effects generally observed at intakes of approximately 60-100 g/day. They also note that evidence certainty varied across outcomes and that sparse data at higher intakes limit firm conclusions regarding dose thresholds.

42727977.summary: This population-based cohort study evaluated the generalisability of cardiovascular disease risk predictor effects across populations from a high-income country versus a non-high-income country. The investigators derived comparable risk prediction equations and explored strategies to improve prediction accuracy across different settings. Primary prevention cohorts of individuals aged 30 to 74 years with diabetes and no prior cardiovascular disease were identified from electronic health records in New Zealand and China. Sex-specific five-year equations incorporating 16 predictors were derived using standardised methods to predict first cardiovascular events. Between 2004 and 2018, the New Zealand cohort included 47,958 participants who experienced 5622 (11.7%) first cardiovascular disease events. Between 2010 and 2018, the Chinese cohort comprised 46,558 participants with 3650 (7.8%) first cardiovascular disease events. Hazard ratios for most predictors were similar between countries, but the hazard ratio for age differed markedly. Specifically, among women, the hazard ratio for age per 10 years was 1.61 (95% confidence interval 1.51 to 1.71) in New Zealand versus 2.51 (95% confidence interval 2.32 to 2.72) in China. When New Zealand equations were applied to the Chinese cohort, standard recalibration did not improve calibration, resulting in expected to observed ratios of 0.938 in men and 0.809 in women. Replacing New Zealand age coefficients with Chinese age coefficients improved model calibration, yielding expected to observed ratios of 1.027 in men and 1.025 in women. The authors noted that applying equations derived from high-income countries to non-high-income populations with diabetes can lead to systematic errors primarily related to age effect differences.
42727977.relation_evidence: Cardiovascular risk prediction tools developed in high-income settings are commonly transported to other populations using simple recalibration. This study demonstrates that standard recalibration may be insufficient when key predictor hazard ratios, particularly for age, vary significantly across different international populations.
42727977.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42727977.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that applying cardiovascular disease risk prediction equations derived from high-income countries to populations with diabetes from non-high-income countries may introduce systematic errors driven by differences in the effect of age, and that updating key predictor coefficients, particularly age, represents a feasible strategy to improve accuracy.

42726053.summary: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a genetic heart disorder characterized by fibrofatty replacement of ventricular myocardium, sustained ventricular arrhythmia (VA), and elevated risk of sudden death. Current clinical guidelines restrict high-intensity aerobic exercise and competitive sports in individuals with ACM or at risk due to pathogenic or likely-pathogenic (P/LP) gene variants. However, the clinical impact of strength-based exercise on arrhythmic risk remains poorly understood. This study sought to evaluate the risk of VA in individuals with ACM and/or P/LP ACM gene variants exposed to strength-based exercise. Participants were identified from the Johns Hopkins ARVC Registry. Exercise exposure was assessed via telephone from age 10 through follow-up. The study stratified participants into four groups: dual athletes, endurance athletes, strength athletes, and sedentary individuals. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were used to visualize the impact of endurance versus strength exercise on VA risk. Cox proportional hazards regression models were performed to test independent associations between strength exercise and VA. The study enrolled 355 individuals with a median age of 34 years. Distribution across exercise categories comprised 55% dual athletes, 26% sedentary individuals, 12% endurance athletes, and 7% strength athletes. The overall lifetime risk of VA was higher in individuals with increased aerobic exercise (dual plus endurance athletes) compared to those without (strength athletes plus sedentary participants). No significant difference in VA risk was observed between dual versus endurance athletes, nor between strength athletes versus sedentary individuals. Furthermore, multivariable Cox regression analysis showed no association between strength training and VA, whereas the risk associated with endurance exercise was significant.
42726053.relation_evidence: Extensive prior evidence has linked high-intensity endurance and aerobic sports to disease progression and ventricular arrhythmias in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. This study contributes observational data specifically differentiating the arrhythmic risk profile of strength-based exercise from aerobic endurance disciplines in this population.
42726053.relation_guidelines: While current guidelines restrict high-intensity aerobic exercise and competitive sports in individuals with ACM or pathogenic gene variants, recommendations regarding strength-based training have remained less clearly defined. The present findings describe observational registry data regarding the lack of association between strength exercise and sustained ventricular arrhythmias.
42726053.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that their study found no association between strength exercise and the risk of sustained ventricular arrhythmia. They state that these findings support individualized risk stratification and shared decision-making in ACM care, while highlighting the need for additional studies to guide recommendations.

key_findings.label: Association of strength training with VA

42758309.summary: The study addresses the diagnostic yield of different atrial fibrillation (AF) screening methodologies and evaluates how patient characteristics influence detection rates. The authors note that AF screening may reduce adverse outcomes through the early initiation of preventive treatment. To examine this question, the investigators conducted an individual participant data meta-analysis across 12 European and North American study cohorts. Statistical analysis was performed using generalized linear mixed models with a random intercept at the study level. The meta-analysis included a total of 34,165 participants who were screened for AF. The mean age of the overall population was 73.4 ± 7.5 years, and 53.5% of the participants were female. The overall screening yield increased progressively with more intensive diagnostic approaches. Single-timepoint screening demonstrated an AF detection yield of 0.83% (95% CI: 0.24–2.87). Intermittent screening, defined as repeated single-timepoint assessments, resulted in a detection yield of 5.06% (95% CI: 3.55–7.17). Short-term continuous monitoring (≤30 days) had a yield of 4.81% (95% CI: 3.79–6.08), whereas long-term continuous monitoring (>30 days) reached a yield of 30.39% (95% CI: 28.06–32.84). Detection was associated with advanced age, male sex, hypertension, and heart failure. Significant interactions were observed between screening approach and age, sex, heart failure, CHADS2 score, and NT-proBNP levels, with risk factors having a stronger influence on single-timepoint screening than on more intensive methods. The authors indicate that further studies assessing clinical outcomes following screening are needed and currently underway.
42758309.relation_evidence: Screening for atrial fibrillation encompasses diverse modalities ranging from single-timepoint evaluations to prolonged continuous rhythm monitoring. This meta-analysis provides comparative yield estimates across these modalities, demonstrating higher diagnostic rates with extended monitoring durations and specific clinical risk profiles.
42758309.relation_guidelines: Current cardiology guidelines discuss opportunistic and systematic screening approaches for atrial fibrillation in targeted populations based on age and clinical risk factors. These findings refine the evidence base by quantifying how specific modalities and risk factor profiles alter diagnostic yield.
42758309.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that AF screening yield varies substantially by patient characteristics and screening approach, with advanced age, male sex, and heart failure independently associated with greater detection, particularly in single-timepoint screening. They state that these findings support tailoring the screening approach to the individual target population in clinical practice.

key_numbers.design: Individual participant data meta-analysis of 12 study cohorts

42758310.summary: Early rhythm control improves cardiovascular outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation, but its effectiveness in patients with cancer remains unclear. This secondary analysis of the EAST-AFNET 4 trial evaluated the effects of cancer history on early rhythm control outcomes. The study compared patients with and without a history of cancer, including individuals with active malignancy and those in remission. Cancer history status was available for 2779 of 2789 trial participants (99.6%). A history of cancer was present in 216 of 2779 patients (7.8%), of whom 19 had active cancer. Baseline characteristics of patients with cancer included a mean age of 73 years, 44% women (n = 95), and a mean CHA2DS2-VASc score of 3.5. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke, or hospitalization for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome. Safety outcomes encompassed a composite of death, stroke, and serious adverse events related to rhythm control, alongside sinus rhythm maintenance at 24 months. Over a follow-up of up to 8.6 years, early rhythm control reduced the primary composite outcome in patients with and without cancer history (p for interaction = .23). Rates of sinus rhythm at 24 months were high in both cohorts (84.9% with cancer vs 81.8% without cancer; p for interaction = .60). In patients with a cancer history, a safety signal emerged, with safety outcomes occurring in 36 of 116 patients (31%; 22 deaths) assigned to early rhythm control versus 20 of 100 patients (20%; 18 deaths) assigned to usual care (p for interaction = .055). The authors noted that this hypothesis-generating finding may represent the play of chance. The authors conclude that early rhythm control appears effective in patients with atrial fibrillation and cancer history but may carry reduced safety, warranting further investigation.
42758310.relation_evidence: The main EAST-AFNET 4 trial demonstrated cardiovascular outcome benefits with early rhythm control across broad atrial fibrillation populations. This secondary analysis contextualizes those findings within the specific subgroup of patients with a history of malignancy, identifying comparable efficacy but a potential safety signal.
42758310.relation_guidelines: Current atrial fibrillation guidelines address early rhythm control strategies for prognostic and symptomatic management. These subgroup findings refine the understanding of rhythm control in cancer survivors and patients with active cancer, though no specific guideline modifications are directly established from this post hoc analysis.
42758310.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that early rhythm control therapy appears effective in patients with atrial fibrillation and a history of cancer but may be less safe than in patients without cancer in this hypothesis-generating analysis, which warrants further research.

secondary.name: Safety outcome in cancer history subgroup

42757920.summary: The background of this study addresses the increasing prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF) alongside shifts in cardiovascular risk factors, AF detection, and oral anticoagulant use, which may have altered the epidemiology of AF-related stroke. The authors note that population-based data on long-term trends remain limited. The study utilized mandatory nationwide registry data from the Atrial Fibrillation in Norway (AFNOR) study spanning the period from 2001 to 2021. Incident stroke cases were defined as the first hospitalization or death due to stroke among individuals aged 15 years or older. Direct standardization was employed to calculate age-standardized incidence rates. Negative binomial regression was used to estimate sex- and age-adjusted incidence rate ratios (IRR). Across the study period, a total of 227 575 incident strokes were identified. Of these incident strokes, 66 795 (29.4%) were AF-related, showing an increase in the proportion of AF-related strokes from 22% in 2001 to 31% in 2021. Non-anticoagulated individuals accounted for 69% of all AF-related ischemic strokes. The overall incidence rate of AF-related ischemic strokes remained stable, shifting from 67.8 per 100 000 person-years in 2001 to 68.4 in 2021 (IRR=1.01; 95% CI, 1.00-1.03), while increasing specifically among individuals aged 15 to 64 years. In contrast, the incidence rate of non-AF ischemic strokes declined from 204.4 to 130.8 (IRR=0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99). For intracerebral hemorrhage, the incidence of AF-related cases in individuals aged 75 years or older increased, driven by anticoagulated patients. The incidence of non-AF intracerebral hemorrhage decreased over the study timeframe (IRR=0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99). No specific study limitations were reported in the abstract.
42757920.relation_evidence: Existing epidemiological evidence indicates that stroke prevention strategies and anticoagulation patterns have evolved over recent decades alongside changing AF prevalence. This nationwide population-based study provides long-term trend data demonstrating divergent incidence trajectories between AF-related and non-AF strokes across different age groups.
42757920.relation_guidelines: The findings reflect established clinical guideline principles emphasizing oral anticoagulation for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and the structured assessment of bleeding risk in elderly populations. They also describe real-world epidemiological patterns relevant to guideline focus areas on AF detection and anticoagulation adherence.
42757920.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that the favorable decline in ischemic stroke incidence from 2001 to 2021 did not include AF-related strokes, with increases observed in AF-related ischemic strokes in younger age groups and AF-related intracerebral hemorrhage in older anticoagulated patients. They state that these findings underscore the need for improved strategies for AF detection and stroke prevention, particularly in younger populations, and greater attention towards management of bleeding risk among older, anticoagulated individuals.

42755708.summary: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) represents an expanding modality for atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation, though lesion durability and recurrence patterns during redo procedures require further characterization. This study was conducted as a substudy of the FRANCE PFA national exhaustive multicentric registry. The authors analyzed 145 patients with arrhythmia recurrence who underwent repeat ablation procedures with three-dimensional electroanatomical mapping following an index AF ablation. Detailed data regarding initial PFA applications were evaluated to assess recurrence types, durable pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) rates, and linear block durability. Documented recurrent arrhythmias comprised AF in 58%, atrial tachycardia in 28%, and typical atrial flutter in 8% of cases. AF recurrence was significantly less frequent when the initial ablation targeted extra-PV areas compared to when it did not (45% versus 71%; P=0.01). When PVI alone was performed, AF was also less frequent when using a 35-mm diameter catheter compared to standard sizing (50% versus 77%; P=0.01). Complete durable PVI across all veins was observed in 42% of patients, with individual PV durability rates ranging from 69% to 76%. Durable roof/posterior wall block was observed in 62% of patients, whereas durable mitral isthmus block was achieved in 31%. The rate of durable PVI increased with the number of applications (P<0.05), reaching 84% when more than 12 applications were delivered. Similarly, durable roof/posterior wall block rates increased to 88% with more than 16 applications (P<0.01). Mitral isthmus block durability remained low at 31% and was not significantly associated with the number of PFA applications. Safety endpoints and complications were not detailed in the abstract. The authors concluded that higher application numbers yielded high rates of durable PVI and roof/posterior wall block, whereas mitral isthmus durability remained poor using the pentaspline PFA catheter.
42755708.relation_evidence: The study provides observational insights into lesion durability and arrhythmia mechanisms during repeat electroanatomical mapping following pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation.
42755708.relation_guidelines: Current AF guidelines establish pulmonary vein isolation as the cornerstone of rhythm control ablation, and these findings descriptively refine understanding regarding pulsed field lesion durability and extra-pulmonary vein lesion sets.
42755708.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that in patients undergoing redo procedures after an initial AF ablation using the pentaspline PFA catheter, AF was less frequently observed when ablation lesions extended beyond the PVs, high rates of durable PVI (>12 applications) and roof/posterior wall block (>16 applications) were achieved with higher application counts, and long-term durability of mitral isthmus block remained poor.

42760106.summary: Identifying patients with left-sided infective endocarditis (LSIE) who benefit from surgical intervention or present prohibitive operative risk remains a clinical challenge. Currently, no widely validated risk models exist to estimate early 30-day mortality across the broader LSIE population, including medically treated patients. This study aimed to develop and externally validate the European Infective Endocarditis (EURO-ENDO) risk score for predicting 30-day mortality in LSIE. The prospective, multicentre ESC-EURObservational Research Programme EURO-ENDO registry included 2171 patients diagnosed with LSIE according to ESC 2015 criteria. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate clinical, biological, microbiological, and imaging variables, followed by internal bootstrap validation. External validation was conducted in an independent temporal cohort of 377 consecutive patients with LSIE from two tertiary centres in Barcelona between 2019 and 2024. Among 2140 registry patients in the final analysis, 254 (11.9%) died within 30 days. Eleven variables independently predicted 30-day mortality: previous stroke/transient ischaemic attack, previous cardiac surgery, heart failure or cardiogenic shock, creatinine >2 mg/dL, vegetations >10 mm, severe regurgitation, abscess, negative blood cultures, Staphylococcus aureus infection, absence of surgical indication, and surgical indication without intention to operate. The model achieved an AUROC of 0.763, Hosmer-Lemeshow p=0.825, and Brier score of 0.09 in the development dataset. In the external cohort, 48 of 377 patients (12.7%) died within 30 days. External validation demonstrated an AUROC of 0.799 (95% CI 0.730 to 0.868), a calibration slope of 1.017, and an expected-to-observed ratio of 1.124. The authors concluded that the model reliably predicts individualised 30-day mortality during initial evaluation.
42760106.relation_evidence: Risk stratification in infective endocarditis has historically relied on surgical risk scores or smaller cohort models that do not universally account for medically treated patients. This study adds a dedicated, externally validated prognostic model derived from a large international prospective registry across the full spectrum of left-sided infective endocarditis.
42760106.relation_guidelines: The findings align with clinical guidelines that emphasise multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team evaluation and early risk stratification based on clinical, microbiological, and echocardiographic features in left-sided infective endocarditis.
42760106.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that the EURO-ENDO risk score, incorporating 11 variables available during initial diagnostic evaluation, accurately predicts individualised 30-day mortality in patients with LSIE and may support early risk stratification, multidisciplinary endocarditis team discussions, and clinical decision-making.

42757917.summary: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) using the Sapien transcatheter heart valve is utilized for high-risk patients with failed mitral bioprosthetic valves or prior surgical mitral valve repairs. Differences in anatomy and procedural complexity between valve-in-valve TMVR (ViV-TMVR) and valve-in-ring TMVR (ViR-TMVR) may influence clinical outcomes. The authors performed a systematic review searching OVID Medline, Embase, SCOPUS, Web of Science, and Cochrane for studies published between 2015 and 2022 comparing both techniques. Eight studies encompassing 1947 patients were analyzed, comprising 1435 patients receiving ViV-TMVR and 512 receiving ViR-TMVR. Patients undergoing ViV-TMVR were older and had a higher baseline comorbidity burden than those receiving ViR-TMVR. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality, evaluated using random-effects models. Secondary endpoints included in-hospital mortality, stroke, acute kidney injury, major bleeding, reintervention, left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and device embolization. No significant difference was observed between groups in 30-day mortality (OR: 0.70 [95% CI: 0.47-1.05]; I2=0%) or in-hospital mortality (OR: 1.05 [95% CI: 0.34-3.21]; I2=3%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, and device embolization also did not differ significantly between ViV-TMVR and ViR-TMVR. However, ViV-TMVR was associated with a significantly lower rate of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (OR: 0.30 [95% CI: 0.18-0.51]). Additionally, ViV-TMVR was associated with reduced rates of reintervention (OR: 0.19 [95% CI: 0.13-0.30]) and acute kidney injury (OR: 0.51 [95% CI: 0.29-0.90]), without significant heterogeneity. Study limitations were not detailed in the abstract. The authors concluded that these findings may inform patient selection and procedural planning for transcatheter mitral valve interventions.
42757917.relation_evidence: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement represents a therapeutic option for patients with failed surgical bioprostheses or prior mitral valve annuloplasty rings who are at high surgical risk. This pooled analysis summarizes comparative procedural and 30-day outcomes between ViV-TMVR and ViR-TMVR cohorts.
42757917.relation_guidelines: Current valvular heart disease guidelines address transcatheter mitral interventions in high-risk patients with failed previous surgical mitral valve repairs or bioprosthetic valves. These findings provide pooled comparative data regarding procedural risks such as left ventricular outflow tract obstruction and reintervention across these two anatomical settings.
42757917.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that compared with ViR-TMVR, ViV-TMVR was associated with lower rates of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, reintervention, and acute kidney injury, whereas mortality and other major complications were comparable.

key_numbers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 8 studies

42757916.summary: Evidence comparing intermediate-term outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) versus surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients with concomitant heart failure and chronic kidney disease remains limited. This retrospective study utilized data from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network between January 2020 and December 2025. The study population included adults with heart failure and chronic kidney disease undergoing either TAVI or SAVR. Patients with redo procedures, history of endocarditis, prior heart transplant, ventricular assist device placement, or concomitant valve surgery were excluded. Before matching, the cohort included 9575 patients who underwent TAVI and 1233 who underwent SAVR. Propensity score matching across 21 covariates yielded 1034 matched patients in each procedural group. The primary outcome was all-cause death evaluated over 2 years of follow-up using Cox proportional hazards models. Secondary outcomes comprised acute myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, acute kidney injury, and all-cause hospitalization. During follow-up, TAVI was associated with a higher mortality rate compared with SAVR (hazard ratio [HR], 1.56 [95% CI, 1.21-2.01]). Conversely, TAVI was associated with a lower risk of acute kidney injury compared with SAVR (HR, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]). Risks of acute myocardial infarction (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.87-1.44]), ischemic stroke (HR, 1.11 [95% CI, 0.85-1.45]), and all-cause hospitalization (HR, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.81-1.00]) did not show statistically significant differences between groups. Sensitivity analyses across alternative modeling strategies demonstrated directionally consistent results. The study abstract did not report specific post-hoc subgroup analyses or unmeasured confounding limitations.
42757916.relation_evidence: The comparative effectiveness of TAVI versus SAVR across complex subgroups with combined cardiorenal disease has been an area of ongoing investigation. These findings contribute observational data on intermediate-term survival and renal outcomes in this specific multimorbid population.
42757916.relation_guidelines: Current valvular heart disease guidelines weigh procedural risks, surgical risk scores, and patient comorbidities when evaluating patients for TAVI versus SAVR. These observational findings describe procedural trade-offs between mortality and renal complications in patients with concomitant heart failure and chronic kidney disease.
42757916.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that in this contemporary-era cohort of patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease, SAVR was associated with a lower mortality rate, whereas TAVI was associated with less acute kidney injury, suggesting important trade-offs between procedural strategies in high-risk cardiorenal populations.

42757893.summary: Traditional occluders for atrial septal defect have limitations, including incomplete endothelialization and challenges in achieving transseptal puncture following implantation. The novel ReAces occluder was designed to address these two specific clinical concerns. This multicenter, randomized, parallel-controlled, noninferiority clinical trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of the ReAces device compared with a traditional Amplatzer-like occluder. A total of 126 patients with atrial septal defects were enrolled and randomized in the study. Sixty-two patients received the ReAces device, while 64 patients were implanted with a traditional occluder. The primary outcome of the investigation was the complete closure rate evaluated at 12 months post-implantation. At the 12-month follow-up, complete closure occurred in 98.4% of patients (61/62) in the trial group and 98.4% of patients (63/64) in the control group. These closure rates demonstrated statistical noninferiority with a 95% confidence interval of -4.4% to 4.3%. Regarding safety, no severe adverse events occurred during the 12 months of follow-up, with the exception of one case of device dislodgement in the trial group. At 12 months, the thickness of the central region of the ReAces device was significantly lower than that of the traditional device (6.8±3.7 mm versus 12.2±5.2 mm, P<0.0001). Additionally, the trial group demonstrated a significantly lower Migraine Disability Assessment score at 1-month follow-up compared to the control group (0.4±2.4 versus 1.4±4.1, P=0.042). The proportion of patients with a nonzero Migraine Disability Assessment score at 1 month was also significantly lower in the trial group (5.6% versus 18.2%, P=0.042). Specific trial limitations were not stated in the abstract. The authors concluded that the efficacy of ReAces was noninferior to that of a traditional occluder, while providing a thinner central region and lower 1-month migraine disability scores.
42757893.relation_evidence: Transcatheter closure using Amplatzer-like occluders represents established management for anatomically suitable atrial septal defects. This trial adds randomized comparative evidence evaluating a novel device design intended to modify device thickness and address post-procedural migraine symptoms.
42757893.relation_guidelines: Current clinical practice guidelines support transcatheter device closure as a standard approach for secundum atrial septal defects with suitable anatomy. These findings provide comparative device-specific noninferiority data without altering established guideline-directed indications for transcatheter defect closure.
42757893.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that the efficacy of ReAces was noninferior to that of a traditional Amplatzer-like occluder for transcatheter atrial septal defect closure. They also conclude that ReAces had a thinner central region during follow-up and a lower Migraine Disability Assessment score at 1-month follow-up.

42757942.summary: The background of this study notes that the impact of the left internal mammary artery (LIMA)-to-left anterior descending artery (LAD) anastomotic location on graft patency remains uncertain. To evaluate this question, investigators conducted a secondary analysis of data from the PATENCY (Graft Patency Between no-touch Vein Harvesting Technique and Conventional Approach in Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery) trial. The study population comprised 1597 patients with isolated proximal LAD lesions who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting. The relative anastomotic site (RAS) of the LIMA-LAD anastomosis was quantified using postoperative coronary computed tomography angiography. RAS was defined as the ratio of anastomotic height to heart height. The primary end point of the study was LIMA occlusion at 3 years. The secondary end point was major adverse cardiac events. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between RAS and 3-year LIMA occlusion. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate associations with time-to-event clinical outcomes. An exploratory RAS threshold was identified at 46%. A distal anastomosis (RAS >46%) was associated with a significantly lower 3-year LIMA occlusion rate compared with a proximal anastomosis (RAS ≤46%) (2.3% versus 6.3%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.20-0.68]; P=0.002). At 3 years, major adverse cardiac event rates were similar between groups (3.4% versus 4.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.40-1.15]; P=0.16). The authors conclude that a more distal LIMA-LAD anastomotic location may be associated with a lower risk of graft occlusion at 3 years in patients with isolated proximal LAD disease and noted that further prospective validation is warranted.
42757942.relation_evidence: Surgical revascularization of the left anterior descending artery using the left internal mammary artery is an established standard in coronary bypass surgery. This analysis provides observational data regarding how the anatomical height of the anastomosis relates to 3-year graft patency.
42757942.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42757942.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that in patients with isolated proximal LAD disease, a more distal LIMA-LAD anastomotic location may be associated with a lower risk of graft occlusion at 3 years, noting that further prospective validation is warranted.

42757900.summary: This cohort study evaluated the real-world effectiveness of evolocumab in reducing major adverse cardiovascular events among US adults with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Patients who initiated evolocumab between 2017 and 2023 were identified using the Komodo Healthcare Map database. At day 75 post-initiation, designated as the index date, individuals were classified into treated and nontreated cohorts. The treated group included patients who remained on evolocumab, whereas the nontreated group comprised patients who discontinued therapy prior to day 75. Patients were followed until outcome occurrence, treatment discontinuation or reinitiation, insurance disenrollment, database termination, or death. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or coronary revascularization. The secondary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular disease death. Four-year cumulative incidence, risk ratios, and 95% confidence intervals were estimated using inverse probability of treatment and censoring weighting. Negative control outcomes were evaluated prior to comparative analyses to assess potential residual confounding. Following weighting, baseline characteristics were balanced between the treated group (n=87 102) and the nontreated group (n=24 609). At 4 years of follow-up, treated patients exhibited a 20% lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with nontreated patients (RR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.73–0.86). For the secondary composite outcome at 4 years, treated patients had a 29% lower risk compared with nontreated patients (RR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.64–0.78). Specific adverse events and safety endpoints were not described in the abstract. The authors concluded that evolocumab use was associated with significant reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events in routine clinical practice.
42757900.relation_evidence: Randomized controlled trials have established that evolocumab reduces major adverse cardiovascular events in secondary prevention populations. This observational analysis adds large-scale real-world data evaluating outcomes associated with continued evolocumab therapy in routine practice.
42757900.relation_guidelines: Clinical practice guidelines recommend PCSK9 inhibitors for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease who require additional lipid-lowering therapy. The reported findings are consistent with guideline-directed secondary prevention strategies utilizing PCSK9 inhibitors.
42757900.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that in a large, diverse, real-world population with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, evolocumab use was associated with significant reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events, supporting the effectiveness of guideline-recommended PCSK9 inhibitor therapy in routine clinical practice.

42757888.summary: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) represents a leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the early postpartum period. Stillbirth has previously been linked to elevated long-term maternal CVD risk, but its relationship with short-term CVD remains less characterized. To investigate this, investigators conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study of singleton delivery hospitalizations using the Nationwide Readmissions Database from 2010 to 2020. The primary outcome was CVD-related readmission or in-hospital death within the calendar year of delivery, encompassing heart disease and stroke. Associations were analyzed using adjusted Cox proportional hazards models with correction for unmeasured confounding. Analyses were also stratified by the presence of chronic hypertension, ischemic placental disease, and diabetes. The study identified 18,253,997 singleton delivery hospitalizations, of which 117,230 (6.5 per 1000) resulted in stillbirth. The median follow-up period was 6.4 months (interquartile range, 3.7-9.1). CVD-related readmission rates were higher after stillbirth than live birth (404.0 versus 166.0 per 100,000 delivery hospitalizations; incidence proportion difference, 238 per 100,000 [95% CI, 192-285]). Stillbirth was associated with higher overall hazards of CVD hospitalization (adjusted HR, 2.03 [95% CI, 1.78-2.32]). Significant hazard increases were observed for heart disease (adjusted HR, 2.00 [95% CI, 1.72-2.32]), stroke (adjusted HR, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.80-2.92]), and CVD-related death (adjusted HR, 2.08 [95% CI, 1.12-3.84]). CVD hospitalization risk was elevated within 30 days postpartum and reached its peak from 60 to 89 days. Hospitalization risks were higher in the presence of co-occurring chronic hypertension, ischemic placental disease, or diabetes. The authors conclude that stillbirth is associated with increased short-term CVD-related readmission and death.
42757888.relation_evidence: Adverse pregnancy outcomes have been widely recognized as markers for accelerated long-term cardiovascular risk in women. This study provides population-level data demonstrating that stillbirth is also associated with an increased risk of acute maternal cardiovascular events and readmissions during the immediate postpartum period.
42757888.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42757888.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that stillbirth was associated with increased short-term CVD-related readmission and death, extending prior evidence linking stillbirth to long-term CVD risk.

42896534.summary: The PELICAN randomized clinical trial investigated whether intraoperative hemodynamic therapy guided by cardiac index improves postoperative outcomes. The trial evaluated individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy compared with routine hemodynamic therapy in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery. This was a multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial conducted at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. Enrollment occurred between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, with final follow-up completed on January 15, 2026. Among 1128 enrolled patients, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis. Participants had a median age of 67 years (interquartile range, 59-74 years), and 49.4% were female. The intervention consisted of individualized hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index, whereas the control group received routine hemodynamic therapy with blinded cardiac index monitoring. The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized therapy group versus 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine therapy group. This difference corresponded to a relative risk of 0.94 (95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08; P = .38). Secondary outcomes assessed the individual components of the composite primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. The trial reported no between-group differences in the incidence of any individual components of the primary outcome. Specific trial-related adverse events and study limitations were not described in the abstract. The authors concluded that individualized cardiac index-guided therapy did not reduce the 7-day composite outcome compared with routine therapy.
42896534.relation_evidence: Perioperative goal-directed hemodynamic protocols have yielded heterogeneous results regarding postoperative complications in major surgery. The PELICAN trial provides multicenter randomized data assessing an individualized strategy targeting preoperative resting cardiac index in high-risk abdominal surgery.
42896534.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42896534.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy.

42895716.summary: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure that disproportionately affects individuals of predominantly African ancestry, in whom familial clustering of disease is more pronounced than in individuals of European ancestry. Truncating variants in TTN represent the most common established monogenic cause of DCM, while a common CD36 nonsense variant enriched in African ancestry also accounts for a substantial disease burden. This multicohort genetic association study evaluated the contribution of a CD36 nonsense variant to DCM risk compared with TTN truncating variants and pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other established DCM genes. The study analyzed exome or genome sequence data from 4 US datasets: the All of Us Research Program, the Million Veteran Program, the Penn Medicine Biobank, and the DCM Precision Medicine Study. Exposures assessed were carrier status for TTN truncating variants, pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 11 high-confidence DCM genes, and 0, 1, or 2 copies of the nonsense variant CD36 Y325*. Across the 4 cohorts, 82,623 individuals of predominantly African ancestry were analyzed, with a mean age of 53.4 years (SD, 13.9 years), 47,124 male participants, and 1,316 cases of DCM. Main outcomes evaluated were the risk of DCM, the prevalence of variant carriers among cases, and the population attributable fraction of DCM. Individuals homozygous for the CD36 Y325* risk allele had a higher risk of DCM, with an odds ratio of 4.8 (95% CI, 3.1-7.3). Heterozygous carriers of CD36 Y325* also exhibited an elevated risk of DCM, with an odds ratio of 1.4 (95% CI, 1.2-1.7). TTN truncating variants conferred an odds ratio of 8.5 (95% CI, 5.5-13.0) for DCM among participants of African ancestry. Among the 1,316 African ancestry DCM cases, 33 (2.5%) were homozygous for CD36, 56 (4.3%) harbored TTN truncating variants, and 16 (1.2%) carried pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other high-confidence DCM genes. In population-level analyses incorporating heterozygous and homozygous carriers, the population attributable fraction for CD36 was 9.0% (6.2% for heterozygous and 2.8% for homozygous carriers), surpassing the 3.7% population attributable fraction for TTN truncating variants. Safety endpoints and adverse events were not evaluated, and study limitations were not reported in the abstract. The authors concluded that an ancestry-specific CD36 variant contributed more to DCM burden among individuals of African ancestry than established DCM genes, reshaping the known genetic architecture of DCM in this population.
42895716.relation_evidence: Existing genetic architecture models for dilated cardiomyopathy identify truncating variants in TTN as the predominant monogenic contributor based largely on studies in European-ancestry populations. This study demonstrates that in individuals of African ancestry, the common CD36 Y325* nonsense variant accounts for a larger population attributable fraction of dilated cardiomyopathy than TTN truncating variants or other established high-confidence genes.
42895716.relation_guidelines: Current cardiomyopathy and heart failure guidelines focus genetic screening recommendations primarily on established rare monogenic variants such as truncating variants in TTN. These findings refine understanding of genetic susceptibility in individuals of African ancestry by highlighting a significant contribution from an ancestry-enriched CD36 variant not routinely featured on standard panels.
42895716.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that in 4 US cohorts, an ancestry-specific CD36 variant contributed more to the dilated cardiomyopathy burden among individuals of African ancestry than established genes for the disease, including TTN truncating variants. They further state that these findings reshape the known genetic architecture of dilated cardiomyopathy in individuals of African ancestry and highlight the importance of representation in genomic research.

42909429.summary: Preeclampsia is reported to increase the long-term risk of heart failure 4-fold, yet universal guidelines for postpartum heart failure surveillance remain lacking. Subclinical stage B heart failure has been shown to predict major adverse cardiac outcomes, and initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage may reduce progression to symptomatic heart failure. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate cardiac structure and function in women with prior preeclampsia and identify the timing of subclinical heart failure development. A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CINAHL was performed according to PRISMA guidelines for studies assessing left ventricular function using transthoracic echocardiography. The analysis included 45 case-control studies encompassing 8,991 women, of whom 2,288 had a history of preeclampsia, compared with normotensive controls. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index, with a standard mean difference of 10.85 (95% CI: 6.30-15.39). They also showed higher relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), elevated E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), and prolonged isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]). Furthermore, preeclamptic women exhibited a lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]). In the postpartum period, global longitudinal strain remained reduced and left ventricular mass index remained elevated out to 10 years postpartum. All other evaluated echocardiographic variables showed no significant differences beyond 6 months postpartum. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained comparable between preeclampsia and control groups at all timepoints. The authors noted that evidence for persistent left ventricular mass index elevation beyond 6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Adverse events were not evaluated as endpoints in this meta-analysis. The authors concluded that preeclampsia is linked to subclinical myocardial dysfunction characterized by impaired global longitudinal strain and increased left ventricular mass index.
42909429.relation_evidence: Preeclampsia is an established female-specific risk factor associated with long-term maternal cardiovascular disease and heart failure. This meta-analysis aggregates echocardiographic data showing that left ventricular structural remodeling and subclinical systolic strain impairment originate during pregnancy and can persist for up to a decade postpartum.
42909429.relation_guidelines: Current guidelines recognize preeclampsia as a condition that enhances cardiovascular risk, though specific postpartum surveillance protocols for subclinical heart failure are not defined. These findings characterize the structural and functional myocardial alterations that could inform definitions of stage B heart failure in this population.
42909429.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction characterized by impaired global longitudinal strain and increased left ventricular mass index, with strain impairment persisting up to 10 years postpartum. They note that persistent mass index elevation beyond 6 months postpartum requires cautious interpretation and that further studies are needed to determine when subclinical dysfunction progresses to clinical heart failure.

42913986.summary: Catheter ablation is known to reduce atrial fibrillation recurrence and improve symptoms and quality of life, but sham-controlled trials have yielded discordant findings. This systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis sought to synthesise sham-controlled trials of catheter ablation and explore reasons for divergent quality-of-life outcomes. Databases and clinical trial registries were searched for randomized trials evaluating catheter ablation versus sham procedures in symptomatic atrial fibrillation. Overall, four randomized trials comprising 468 patients met the inclusion criteria, and three trials including 448 patients were pooled for quantitative synthesis. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) score, evaluated using a Bayesian random-effects model. Catheter ablation improved the AFEQT score relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval 1.6 to 26.9). The posterior probability of achieving benefit was 0.98, and the posterior probability of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference was 0.94. Using the primary estimator from the PVI-SHAM-AF trial, the between-group difference was 12.9 points (95% credible interval -0.4 to 27.1), with posterior probabilities of 0.97 for benefit and 0.91 for exceeding the minimal clinically important difference. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (tau 8.2 points, I2 85.3%), which was largely attributed to the PVI-SHAM-AF trial due to differences in symptom severity, rhythm monitoring, and blinding assessment. Excluding PVI-SHAM-AF resulted in a between-group AFEQT score difference of 18.9 points (95% credible interval 6.7 to 31.4). Catheter ablation reduced atrial fibrillation recurrence across all included trials, with a pooled risk ratio of 0.49 (95% credible interval 0.17 to 0.89). GRADE assessment indicated moderate certainty of evidence for atrial fibrillation burden and recurrence, but low certainty for quality of life. The abstract did not report safety or adverse event data. The authors concluded that catheter ablation reduces recurrence and burden and exhibits a high probability of clinically important quality-of-life benefit compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control.
42913986.relation_evidence: Substantial evidence demonstrates that catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation burden and recurrence compared with medical therapy, though recent sham-controlled trials reported conflicting quality-of-life results. This meta-analysis aggregates the sham-controlled trial evidence to quantify treatment effects beyond the placebo response.
42913986.relation_guidelines: Current atrial fibrillation guidelines incorporate catheter ablation as an established strategy to alleviate symptoms and reduce arrhythmia episodes in symptomatic patients. The findings of this meta-analysis are consistent with these guideline frameworks regarding reductions in recurrence and burden, while characterizing the remaining uncertainty around the exact magnitude of sham-controlled quality-of-life gains.
42913986.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation recurrence and burden and carries a high probability of clinically important quality-of-life benefit, despite remaining uncertainty about its exact magnitude. They add that differences between trials reflect variation in population characteristics, rhythm monitoring methods, and statistical estimators rather than divergent directions of treatment effect.

42909425.summary: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) procedure time but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium. The randomized Q-INDEX trial was conducted to compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. In this multicenter, open-label study, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three ablation strategies using the QDOT MICRO catheter. The first group received AI-guided ablation targeting an AI of 500 on anterior segments and 400 elsewhere. The second group received a hybrid strategy using AI-guided ablation on anterior segments (AI 500) and vHPSD elsewhere. The third group underwent uniform vHPSD ablation at 90 W/4 sec across all segments. The primary endpoint was total ablation time, and secondary endpoints included acute pulmonary vein reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia. Acute pulmonary vein isolation was achieved in all enrolled patients. Total ablation time differed significantly, being longest with AI-guided ablation and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 pulmonary vein segments occurred in 7.7% of the AI-guided group, 9.4% of the hybrid group, and 10.6% of the vHPSD group (P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6% across the groups, respectively (log-rank P = .13; P = .049 for AI-guided vs vHPSD). Regarding safety, no cardiac tamponade occurred, steam pops occurred exclusively in the 90 W groups, and two minor periprocedural strokes occurred in the vHPSD group with subsequent full recovery. The rate of silent cerebral lesions detected on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ significantly among the groups at 5%, 10%, and 0% (P = .35). The authors noted that the study was powered for ablation time and that these exploratory findings warrant confirmation.
42909425.relation_evidence: Pulmonary vein isolation is the standard ablation approach for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, with diverse power and duration parameters utilized to achieve durable transmural lesions. This randomized study provides comparative evidence regarding procedural efficiency, safety events, and 1-year clinical durability between standard ablation index guidance, very high-power short-duration ablation, and a regional hybrid strategy.
42909425.relation_guidelines: Current atrial fibrillation guidelines establish pulmonary vein isolation as the recommended target for catheter ablation without prescribing a specific radiofrequency power-time formulation. The findings describe how differing lesion depth strategies perform within standard pulmonary vein isolation procedures.
42909425.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. They further conclude that these exploratory findings support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

42900029.summary: Unexplained cardiac arrest associated with idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF) represents a heterogeneous entity causing notable mortality in young individuals. This retrospective multicenter cohort study investigated the natural history, recurrence burden, emerging etiologies, and long-term management of IVF survivors across 46 tertiary centers. Eligible participants were older than 15 years, presented with documented ventricular fibrillation, had extensive negative initial evaluations supporting IVF, and completed at least 5 years of follow-up. Patient outcomes were compiled from medical records, follow-up testing, genetic evaluations, and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator data. The cohort comprised 825 patients (37% women, mean age 35.7 ± 12 years) followed for a median duration of 120 months. All-cause death occurred in 27 patients (3.3%), including cardiac death in 1.2%, noncardiac death in 1.1%, and unknown causes in 1.0%, while 4.5% developed overt cardiomyopathy. Overall arrhythmia recurrences accumulated steadily across two decades to affect 52.7% of patients, with a median time to first recurrence of 20 months and similar rates between sexes. Emergent etiologies were identified in 68.8% of the total cohort based on recurrence data, structural evolution, genetic findings, and electrophysiologic mapping. These etiologies included focal sources in 33.0%, microstructural myocardial alterations (MiCM) with normal imaging in 27.0%, and reclassified inherited arrhythmia conditions in 8.8%, whereas 31.2% remained without an identified diagnosis. In subgroup comparisons, focal IVF involved more female patients, presented more frequently during rest or sleep, and demonstrated narrower QRS durations than MiCM (90.1 ± 12 ms vs 104.8 ± 16 ms; P < 0.001). Quinidine appeared effective in preventing focal IVF in 68.3% of treated cases, whereas beta-blockers appeared effective in 49.3% of MiCM-IVF cases. Catheter ablation was performed in 181 patients, among whom 75.7% had no subsequent recurrence. Study limitations were not detailed in the abstract. The authors concluded that IVF survivors demonstrate low cardiac mortality alongside persistent long-term recurrence risks, frequently revealing emerging etiologies over extended surveillance.
42900029.relation_evidence: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation is historically understood as unexplained ventricular fibrillation without detectable structural or electrical disease at baseline. These findings add descriptive evidence that over a median 10-year follow-up, late diagnostic emergence and structural or electrophysiologic reclassification occur in a majority of surviving patients.
42900029.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42900029.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that long-term follow-up of idiopathic ventricular fibrillation survivors demonstrates low cardiac mortality alongside a persistent risk of arrhythmia recurrences over time, and identifies potential emerging etiologies.

42919988.summary: Cardiac pacing has undergone a shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing toward physiological activation of the native conduction system. Chronic right ventricular pacing has been shown to induce ventricular dyssynchrony, which contributes to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network of the heart to preserve or restore the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing represents the earliest form of conduction system pacing and provided proof of concept for the field. His bundle pacing is nonetheless limited by technical challenges as well as high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has since emerged as the dominant conduction system pacing modality. This modality provides greater procedural success, improved lead stability, and broader clinical applicability. Applications of left bundle branch area pacing span bradycardia management, prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, and cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is described as an emerging atrial counterpart to ventricular physiological pacing. Capturing this preferential interatrial conduction pathway reduces interatrial conduction delay compared with conventional right atrial appendage pacing. This atrial approach produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence and might help prevent atrial fibrillation. The review unites ventricular and atrial modalities under the shared principle of physiological pacing. The authors examine the mechanistic basis, technical evolution, and latest evidence from randomized trials across these modalities. Practical considerations in clinical application are addressed, and areas requiring further evidence are highlighted.
42919988.relation_evidence: Conduction system pacing, including His bundle pacing and left bundle branch area pacing, represents a shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing to avoid pacing-induced dyssynchrony and cardiomyopathy. The exploration of Bachmann bundle area pacing extends physiological pacing principles to the atrium to reduce interatrial conduction delays.
42919988.relation_guidelines: The review's appraisal of left bundle branch area pacing aligns with the evolving interest in physiological pacing strategies across contemporary pacing and heart failure guidelines. Specific guideline links for Bachmann bundle area pacing cannot be derived from the abstract alone.
42919988.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that ventricular and atrial conduction system pacing approaches fall under a unifying principle of physiological pacing that improves activation patterns, while noting that practical clinical application requires further evidence in specific areas.

42918521.summary: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), represents a physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data have been limited. The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) observational registry evaluated the feasibility, predictors of procedural failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP. A total of 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP across 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025 were enrolled. Capture types were classified in accordance with European Heart Rhythm Association criteria. Procedures were predominantly performed using stylet-driven leads, which were utilized in 87.0% of cases. Overall CSP procedural success was documented in 87.4% of patients (1,932 of 2,211). Among the 1,922 patients receiving LBBAP, left bundle branch pacing was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, a right-sided approach, and male sex were identified as independent predictors of CSP failure. Pacing parameters remained stable over a mean follow-up of 17.0 ± 10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but this association lost statistical significance after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization compared with left bundle branch pacing plus left fascicular pacing (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05–8.73, p = 0.039). The authors noted that this heart-failure finding was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not statistically significant on unadjusted analysis. The authors conclude that LBBAP was feasible and safe in this cohort, with direct conduction capture showing an association with lower adjusted heart-failure hospitalizations.
42918521.relation_evidence: Conduction system pacing, including left bundle branch area pacing, is increasingly investigated as an alternative to conventional myocardial pacing to preserve ventricular synchrony. This registry adds observational evidence on procedural feasibility, success rates, and lead characteristics within a large Asian cohort.
42918521.relation_guidelines: Current cardiology guidelines discuss physiologic pacing modalities, such as conduction system pacing, as potential alternatives to conventional ventricular pacing in selected clinical scenarios. These observational findings describe real-world procedural characteristics and capture types without altering current guideline recommendations.
42918521.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that LBBAP was feasible and safe in this large-scale Asian registry, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. They further state that direct conduction system capture was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, noting that these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

42913987.summary: The Omny-IRE study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact-force-sensing, pulsed field ablation basket catheter integrated with electroanatomic mapping. The objective was to report 12-month outcomes following pulmonary vein isolation using the OMNYPULSE platform in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Follow-up through the 12-month visit incorporated electrocardiography preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Rhythm surveillance further included 24-hour Holter monitoring at 3, 6, and 12 months, as well as remote rhythm monitoring performed weekly during months 1 to 5, monthly during months 6 to 12, and upon symptom triggers. The secondary effectiveness endpoint was 12-month freedom from documented symptomatic or asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia lasting 30 seconds or longer and acute procedural failure. Additional evaluated outcomes included device- and procedure-related serious adverse events, Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life scores, and healthcare utilization. Among 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main-phase cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In the main-phase cohort, 12-month freedom from symptomatic or asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5%, which was 90.1% when assessed using standard-of-care monitoring only. Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device- or procedure-related serious adverse events were reported in 2.9% of main-phase patients. Patient-reported quality of life improved, with a mean increase in overall AFEQT score of 25.5 points from baseline to 12 months. Healthcare utilization declined, with cardiovascular hospitalizations decreasing by 40.9% compared with the 12-month preprocedure period. In addition, Class I/III antiarrhythmic drug use decreased by 49.3% between 6 and 12 months postablation compared with baseline. Study limitations were not described in the abstract.
42913987.relation_evidence: Catheter ablation utilizing pulsed field ablation represents an evolving non-thermal approach to achieve pulmonary vein isolation in atrial fibrillation. This study provides prospective 12-month data regarding procedural outcomes and safety for a contact-force-sensing, focal multielectrode pulsed field ablation platform with electroanatomic mapping integration.
42913987.relation_guidelines: Current clinical practice guidelines recognize catheter ablation for pulmonary vein isolation as an established rhythm control strategy in symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. These findings report observational 12-month safety and effectiveness metrics for a specific pulsed field ablation system within this clinical context.
42913987.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and healthcare benefits of pulsed field ablation with the OMNYPULSE platform.

42913970.summary: Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures can emerge years after implantation. This study was conducted to evaluate the 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure defibrillation lead in a real-world Medicare population. Investigators linked manufacturer device-tracking records to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. The analysis included patients receiving an Optisure lead between February 2014 and December 2024. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims requiring both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario incorporating confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario incorporating both confirmed and potentially related events. The study cohort comprised 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. The mean age of the population was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillators. During follow-up, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related, and 606 were classified as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% CI, 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario. In the worst-case scenario, 10-year complication-free survival was 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%). Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type. Specific study limitations were not stated in the abstract. The authors conclude that the Optisure lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice, supporting its durability and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market surveillance.
42913970.relation_evidence: Transvenous defibrillator leads are known to be vulnerable to mechanical failure and insulation degradation over extended periods of follow-up. This study provides long-term real-world performance data on a specific multi-layer insulated lead design across a 10-year timeframe.
42913970.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42913970.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that the Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice, supporting both its long-term durability and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

42925297.summary: Whether age influences the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization versus staged complete revascularization during index admission for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction with multivessel disease remains unknown. The authors conducted a secondary analysis of the randomized OPTION-STEMI trial to evaluate the impact of age on clinical outcomes. The trial cohort comprised 994 patients randomized to either immediate complete revascularization or in-hospital staged complete revascularization. Complete revascularization of non-infarct-related arteries was guided by fractional flow reserve. The primary endpoint evaluated at 1 year was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization. Outcomes were analyzed according to patient age and complete revascularization strategy. Analysis of age as a continuous variable revealed a statistically significant interaction with revascularization strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The hazard ratio for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged complete revascularization arm until approximately 67 years of age. Above 67 years of age, the hazard ratio increased steadily in the immediate complete revascularization arm. In binary subgroup analysis, patients aged 70 years or older had a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint with immediate versus staged complete revascularization (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029). In patients younger than 70 years, no significant difference between strategies was observed (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470). The multiplicative interaction P value was 0.054, and the relative excess risk due to interaction P value was 0.016. Additional safety endpoints and study limitations were not reported in the abstract. The authors note that these findings warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials.
42925297.relation_evidence: Complete revascularization reduces adverse cardiovascular events in patients presenting with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease. However, the optimal timing of non-culprit lesion intervention—whether immediate during primary percutaneous coronary intervention or staged during the index hospitalization—across specific patient subsets such as older adults remains an unresolved question.
42925297.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42925297.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate complete revascularization compared with in-hospital staged complete revascularization. They state that age modifies the treatment effect of the complete revascularization strategy, warranting confirmation in adequately powered trials.

42900708.summary: Coronary bifurcation lesions represent a technically challenging subset of percutaneous coronary interventions, with suboptimal clinical outcomes frequently observed in side branches. Drug-coated balloons have demonstrated acceptable clinical outcomes in native coronary artery disease. The OCVC-BIF study was conducted as a multicenter, randomized, open-label trial designed to assess the efficacy and safety of supplementary drug-coated balloon inflation in the side branches of bifurcation lesions. Eligible patients had coronary bifurcation lesions scheduled for drug-eluting stent implantation in the main vessel followed by kissing balloon inflation. Participants were randomized to either additional side-branch dilatation with a drug-coated balloon following drug-eluting stent implantation and kissing balloon inflation or standard drug-eluting stent implantation with conventional kissing balloon inflation alone. The primary end point was side-branch restenosis, defined as at least 50% stenosis assessed by three-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography on scheduled 9-month angiography or symptom-driven angiography through 1-year follow-up. The key secondary end point was major adverse cardiac events at 12 months, comprising cardiac death, myocardial infarction, clinically driven target lesion revascularization, and stent thrombosis. Between October 2019 and September 2024, a total of 299 patients were enrolled, with 151 allocated to the drug-coated balloon group and 148 to the non-drug-coated balloon group. Serial three-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography was completed in 262 patients, representing 87.6% of the trial cohort. The primary end point of side-branch restenosis occurred in 8.1% of patients in the drug-coated balloon group compared with 18.3% in the non-drug-coated balloon group (P=0.012). At 12 months, the incidence of major adverse cardiac events was 10.1% in the drug-coated balloon group and 12.4% in the non-drug-coated balloon group (P=0.58). Specific trial limitations were not detailed in the abstract. The authors conclude that additional drug-coated balloon inflation in the side branch after main-vessel drug-eluting stent implantation with kissing balloon inflation reduces side-branch restenosis in bifurcation lesions.
42900708.relation_evidence: Bifurcation interventions frequently encounter side-branch compromise and restenosis after provisional or complex stenting strategies. Drug-coated balloons deliver antiproliferative agents locally without requiring permanent scaffold implantation in the side branch.
42900708.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42900708.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that additional DCB inflation in the side branch after main-vessel DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation decreases restenosis in the side branch in the treatment of bifurcation lesions.
