42910974.summary: The optimal clinical management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation remains uncertain. This study comprised a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials comparing routine coronary revascularisation with conservative management in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation. A network meta-analysis was also performed to evaluate the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies, specifically angiography-guided and physiology-guided percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary outcome of the meta-analysis was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events. Secondary endpoints included all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding. Overall, five trials involving 1,644 patients met the inclusion criteria for the systematic review. Four trials encompassing 1,476 patients contributed data to the primary quantitative synthesis. Compared with conservative management, routine percutaneous coronary intervention significantly reduced the primary composite of major adverse cardiovascular events (risk ratio 0.80, 95% confidence interval: 0.65-0.98). Routine percutaneous coronary intervention was also associated with a reduced incidence of unplanned revascularisation (risk ratio 0.30, 95% confidence interval: 0.11-0.83). Regarding safety events, routine revascularisation was associated with an increased risk of major bleeding compared with conservative management (risk ratio 1.57, 95% confidence interval: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided percutaneous coronary intervention significantly decreased major adverse cardiovascular events, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative management. Among all evaluated revascularisation strategies, physiology-guided percutaneous coronary intervention ranked highest for all ischaemic endpoints. Specific study limitations were not described in the abstract. The authors concluded that routine revascularisation reduces ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative therapy in patients referred for transcatheter aortic valve implantation, with physiology-guided intervention demonstrating the most favourable efficacy profile.
42910974.relation_evidence: The management of concomitant coronary artery disease in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation has historically yielded conflicting observational and randomised evidence regarding the benefits of routine revascularisation. This meta-analysis aggregates randomised trial data to delineate the clinical trade-off between ischaemic risk reduction and post-procedural bleeding complications. It also contextualises the comparative performance of physiology-guided strategies against angiography-guided and conservative approaches.
42910974.relation_guidelines: Current valvular heart disease guidelines address the management of coronary artery disease in patients evaluated for transcatheter aortic valve implantation, where indications for percutaneous intervention remain an area of ongoing debate. These meta-analytic findings add randomised evidence regarding the balance of ischaemic and bleeding events, as well as the role of physiology-guided decision-making in this cohort.
42910974.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that among patients referred for transcatheter aortic valve implantation, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. They further conclude that physiology-guided percutaneous coronary intervention may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies in this setting.

42924854.summary: This study evaluated postoperative neurologic and mortality outcomes according to stroke-to-surgery timing and stroke phenotype in patients with left-sided infective endocarditis. The authors analyzed adult patients who underwent surgery for infective endocarditis complicated by preoperative stroke between 2004 and 2024 across two institutions. The study cohort was stratified by stroke-to-surgery intervals of less than 1 week, 1 to 4 weeks, and 4 to 6 weeks. The primary outcome was a composite postoperative cerebrovascular event comprising new stroke, enlarging stroke, or hemorrhagic conversion. Secondary outcomes assessed included operative death and major morbidity events. Among 2265 screened patients with left-sided infective endocarditis, 322 met the inclusion criteria. In this cohort, 122 patients (38%) had surgery within 1 week, 168 (52%) between 1 and 4 weeks, and 32 (10%) between 4 and 6 weeks. Operative death did not differ significantly across the timing groups (P=0.09). Postoperative cerebrovascular events occurred in 21.3% of patients operated within 1 week, 11.9% at 1 to 4 weeks, and 9.4% at 4 to 6 weeks (P=0.015). On multivariable analysis, a longer stroke-to-surgery interval was associated with reduced odds of postoperative cerebrovascular events (odds ratio, 0.92 per day [95% CI, 0.85-0.98]; P=0.015). This reduction was driven by early events among patients presenting with intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli. Among patients with ischemic stroke, operative death was lowest with surgery within 1 week at 5.8%, compared to 11.2% at 1 to 4 weeks (P=0.24). Interval embolization occurred in 10.6% of patients awaiting surgery, predominantly affecting the spleen and kidneys. Specific study limitations were not described in the abstract.
42924854.relation_evidence: Surgical timing for patients with infective endocarditis complicated by stroke involves balancing the risk of secondary neurologic deterioration against the risk of recurrent systemic embolization and clinical deterioration. Observational literature has historically debated the duration of surgical delay, particularly regarding differences between ischemic and hemorrhagic cerebral events.
42924854.relation_guidelines: Current endocarditis guidelines delineate distinct surgical timing recommendations depending on whether a preoperative stroke is ischemic or hemorrhagic, frequently endorsing early surgery for non-severe ischemic events while favoring delays for intracranial hemorrhage. The findings refine existing guideline frameworks by demonstrating that excess early postoperative cerebrovascular risk is largely restricted to hemorrhagic and septic embolic subtypes rather than ischemic strokes.
42924854.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that excess postoperative neurologic risk was concentrated within the first 7 to 10 days and driven by intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli, with ischemic stroke showing no appreciable temporal association. They state that routine delay after ischemic stroke may not be necessary, whereas a short delay of approximately 7 days for hemorrhagic and septic embolic subtypes may be reasonable when hemodynamically feasible.

42924766.summary: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be technically more challenging in noncentral regions of the mitral valve as well as in anterior or bileaflet lesions. This study evaluated the influence of implant location and leaflet lesion location on the 30-day safety and effectiveness of the PASCAL Precision system in patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation. Data were analyzed from patients treated with the PASCAL Precision system between September 2022 and October 2024 within the US STS/ACC TVT Registry. Outcomes were categorized by implant location into A2P2 and non-A2P2 cohorts, and by leaflet lesion location into anterior, posterior, and bileaflet cohorts. At 30 days, both the A2P2 group (n=1526) and the non-A2P2 group (n=299) demonstrated low adverse event rates, including cardiovascular mortality (1.1% versus 1.0%), mitral valve reintervention (0.4% versus 0.0%), and single leaflet device attachment (0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05). Both implant location cohorts showed significant mitral regurgitation reduction from baseline (P<0.001) without significant difference between groups (P=0.750). Mitral regurgitation ≤2+ was achieved in 93.4% of the A2P2 cohort versus 95.4% of the non-A2P2 cohort, while mitral regurgitation ≤1+ was achieved in 72.0% versus 73.3%. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both implant location groups (mean change of 19.3 versus 17.7 points; P=0.741). In the lesion location analysis, anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also demonstrated low rates of cardiovascular mortality (0.4%, 1.1%, and 0.0%), mitral valve reintervention (0.8%, 0.1%, and 0.5%), and single leaflet device attachment (0.8%, 0.2%, and 0.5%; all P>0.05). Significant mitral regurgitation reduction occurred across all lesion groups (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant intergroup difference (P=0.459), yielding mitral regurgitation ≤2+ rates of 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%, and mitral regurgitation ≤1+ rates of 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved across anterior, posterior, and bileaflet groups (mean change of 21.4, 18.8, and 12.0 points; P=0.087). Limitations were not explicitly detailed in the abstract. The authors concluded that treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days in real-world degenerative mitral regurgitation regardless of implant or lesion location.
42924766.relation_evidence: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair was historically established primarily in central A2P2 pathology, with noncentral and complex leaflet morphologies considered anatomically challenging. These observational findings from the STS/ACC TVT Registry provide descriptive real-world evidence indicating comparable short-term technical and clinical outcomes across central and noncentral implant sites and diverse leaflet lesion locations.
42924766.relation_guidelines: Current valvular heart disease guidelines describe transcatheter edge-to-edge repair as an option for symptomatic severe primary mitral regurgitation in patients who are inoperable or at high surgical risk and fulfill criteria for anatomical suitability. The reported findings descriptively add real-world registry experience on outcomes across various anatomical locations, without altering established guideline criteria.
42924766.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that in real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

42913976.summary: This study evaluated the prognostic importance of atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern on residual clinical risk following left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) and examined whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup. The authors analyzed 3,459 patients with documented AF patterns undergoing LAAO within a contemporary multicenter registry. AF pattern was categorized into paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent AF. Baseline differences across groups were adjusted using inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods. Follow-up imaging was utilized to identify the presence of PDL and DRT. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding assessed by win ratio. After inverse probability weighting, persistent AF and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF, with win ratios of 1.39 and 1.59, respectively. Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with a higher risk of stroke compared with paroxysmal AF (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50). The study observed no significant increase in mortality or major bleeding associated with non-paroxysmal AF. Both PDL and DRT occurred more frequently in patients with non-paroxysmal AF. In the subgroup of patients with PDL or DRT, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with an increased risk of first stroke/SE (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34). This elevated risk in the PDL/DRT subgroup was concentrated between 180 and 540 days after the procedure. The authors concluded that AF pattern independently stratifies residual clinical risk after LAAO, primarily driven by thromboembolism.
42913976.relation_evidence: Existing literature demonstrates that AF pattern influences thromboembolic risk during oral anticoagulation, but its prognostic role after percutaneous LAAO has been less defined. This registry study provides comparative observational data showing that residual thromboembolic risk after LAAO remains higher in non-paroxysmal AF relative to paroxysmal AF.
42913976.relation_guidelines: Current ESC AF guidelines outline indications for LAAO and post-procedure surveillance without differentiating surveillance intervals or procedural indications by AF temporal pattern. These findings describe post-implantation risk stratification across AF patterns without directly altering established guideline frameworks.
42913976.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF driven primarily by thromboembolism. They note that the risk in the PDL/DRT subgroup was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.

42913972.summary: Ventricular arrhythmias often complicate acute coronary syndromes. The prognostic impact of the timing of ventricular arrhythmias relative to percutaneous coronary intervention has remained unclear. The authors conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of observational studies to evaluate this relationship. The analyzed population consisted of acute coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention with or without ventricular arrhythmias, defined as sustained or hemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation. Endpoints evaluated in the analysis were short-term mortality, defined as 30-day or in-hospital death, and long-term mortality at one year. A network meta-analysis compared ventricular arrhythmias occurring before, during, and after percutaneous coronary intervention, using patients without ventricular arrhythmias as the reference group. The analysis synthesized data across 12 observational studies comprising 49,963 patients. A total of 3,475 patients (7.0%) experienced ventricular arrhythmias across the included cohorts. Ventricular arrhythmias were associated with increased short-term mortality (OR 5.04, 95% CI 3.78-6.72). Ventricular arrhythmias were also associated with increased long-term mortality (OR 2.92, 95% CI 2.20-3.86). Among patients who survived to discharge or 30 days, subsequent long-term mortality risk did not significantly differ between patients with and without ventricular arrhythmias (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.62-1.52). The network meta-analysis indicated that all timing categories of ventricular arrhythmias were associated with a significantly higher mortality risk compared with no ventricular arrhythmias. Sensitivity analysis showed that ventricular arrhythmias occurring after percutaneous coronary intervention were associated with higher short-term mortality than earlier ventricular arrhythmias (OR 3.37, 95% CI 1.46-7.82). The authors conclude that ventricular arrhythmias substantially increase death risk in acute coronary syndromes undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention, with post-procedural arrhythmias carrying the highest risk.
42913972.relation_evidence: Ventricular arrhythmias occurring during acute coronary syndromes have historically been associated with adverse short-term outcomes. This meta-analysis adds granular evidence regarding the prognostic significance of the timing of these arrhythmias relative to revascularization, identifying post-PCI arrhythmias as having the highest short-term mortality.
42913972.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42913972.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that ventricular arrhythmias substantially increase the risk of death in patients with acute coronary syndromes undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention, with mortality risk linked to the timing of arrhythmia occurrence and post-PCI arrhythmias conferring the highest risk.

42912400.summary: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is an established tool for assessing cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic significance in young adults remains unclear. This cohort study evaluated the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis. The investigators analyzed the CAC Consortium dataset, consisting of retrospectively assembled data from four United States centers including individuals referred for clinically indicated CAC scans. The study population comprised 12,847 adults aged 30 to 45 years who were followed for a median duration of 22.6 years. The mean (SD) age of the cohort was 40.5 (3.6) years, and 9922 participants (77.2%) were male. At baseline, 9262 individuals (72.1%) had a CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a CAC score between 75% and 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a CAC score greater than 90%. Over the follow-up period, 624 total deaths were documented, including 149 CVD deaths and 81 CHD deaths. In multivariable models adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors, a CAC score greater than 90% compared with a CAC score of 0 was associated with an adjusted hazard ratio of 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27) for all-cause mortality. The adjusted hazard ratio for CVD mortality was 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82) for individuals with a CAC score greater than 90% versus a CAC score of 0. For CHD mortality, the adjusted hazard ratio for a CAC score greater than 90% versus a CAC score of 0 was 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16). Modeled 30-year cumulative incidence demonstrated an all-cause mortality risk of 12.9% in the CAC score greater than 90% group compared with 7.5% in the CAC score 0 group. The modeled 30-year CVD mortality risk was 4.5% versus 1.5%, and CHD mortality risk was 3.0% versus 0.6% for participants with a CAC score greater than 90% compared to those with a CAC score of 0. Specific adverse events and study limitations were not described in the abstract. The authors concluded that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% have a significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality.
42912400.relation_evidence: Coronary artery calcium scoring is well recognized for cardiovascular risk stratification in middle-aged and older populations, but evidence tracking long-term outcomes over multiple decades in young adults has historically been limited.
42912400.relation_guidelines: No clear guideline link can be derived.
42912400.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, suggesting potential implications for guiding the intensification of preventive intervention in this high-risk phenotype.

42924847.summary: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), but its prognostic relevance across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) continuum remains uncertain. The investigators evaluated whether Lp(a) was associated with incident ASCVD across CKM stages and whether it provided risk stratification beyond CKM staging alone. The study cohort comprised 333,321 UK Biobank participants free of clinical cardiovascular disease at baseline. Participants were categorized into CKM stages 0 through 3. Elevated Lp(a) was pre-specified as a concentration of 125 nmol/L or higher. The primary outcome was incident ASCVD, defined as coronary artery disease or ischemic stroke. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to calculate hazard ratios, and 10-year absolute risks were estimated via Kaplan-Meier methods. Over a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 17,581 incident ASCVD events were recorded. After multivariable adjustment for demographic characteristics, socioeconomic factors, lifestyle factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, medications, and CKM stage, elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher ASCVD risk (hazard ratio, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.25-1.36]). In joint analyses, ASCVD risk increased progressively across combined CKM-Lp(a) categories. The highest risk was identified in individuals with CKM stage 3 and elevated Lp(a) compared with those having CKM stage 0 and lower Lp(a) (hazard ratio, 3.43 [95% CI, 2.74-4.31]). Ten-year absolute ASCVD risk spanned from 0.64% to 16.30% across the cohorts. The absolute risk difference associated with elevated Lp(a) increased from 0.23% in stage 0 to 2.20% in stage 3. The authors concluded that elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher incident ASCVD risk across the CKM continuum, with absolute risk increments being greater at more advanced CKM stages.
42924847.relation_evidence: Lp(a) is recognized as an independent, genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in the general population. 42924847.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher incident ASCVD risk across the CKM continuum. They report that although relative associations were broadly consistent across CKM stages, absolute risk increments associated with elevated Lp(a) were greater at more advanced CKM stages, which they describe as lending support to integrating Lp(a) into CKM-based risk stratification for primary prevention.
